messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English between two longtime adult friends sitting together after a difficult day. One friend is quieter than usual and clearly has something on their mind, but they are not ready to explain it. Let the emotion come through naturally through dialogue, pauses, physical behavior, and what they choose not to say. Do not directly explain the characters' emotions to the reader. Keep the scene grounded, restrained, and contemporary. Avoid melodrama, clichés, and a dramatic resolution.

Jordan turned the mug slowly between her hands.

Alex watched her for a moment. “You don't have to talk about it.”

“I know.”

The room stayed quiet for a few seconds.

Jordan took a sip and made a face.

“Too hot?” Alex asked.

“Too bitter.”

“You put three spoonfuls of sugar in it.”

“I was optimistic.”

Alex smiled. “That's your first mistake.”

Jordan looked down at the mug again. “Probably.”

Alex leaned back in the chair and let the silence settle.

A minute passed.

Jordan said, “I thought I was handling everything pretty well.”

Alex didn't answer right away.

“Then something happened today,” Jordan continued, “and suddenly I wasn't.”

Alex nodded once.

Jordan rubbed her thumb along the edge of the mug. “I don't even know what I'm supposed to do with that.”

“You don't have to do anything with it tonight.”

Jordan glanced over.

“Seriously,” Alex said. “You can just have a bad day.”

Jordan looked at her for a long moment.

“That's it?”

“That's it.”

Jordan let out a quiet breath that almost sounded like a laugh.

“I thought you were going to give me some terrible advice.”

“I had some ready.”

“I knew it.”

“But I figured you'd ignore it anyway.”

“I probably would.”

Alex reached over and nudged the sugar jar closer.

Jordan looked at it.

“You still hate bitter coffee?” Alex asked.

“Always.”

“Good. At least some things are still predictable.”

Jordan added another spoonful of sugar.

This time, she smiled.”
